content.text: Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on April 25, 2025, the area sown under the Summer crops is 73.08 lakh ha as compared to 63.34 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. Of this, area of 31.67 lakh ha has been sown under rice this year against the previous year area of 27.64 lakh ha (increase of 4.03 lakh ha). 2. Rabi harvesting Status: As on 25.04.2025, 92.19% of Rabi sown area has been harvested all over India. Approximately 99.00% area of Pulses mainly in Gram (99%), Kulthi (100%), Urdbean (99%), Moongbean (98%); 87.99% area of Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals mainly in Jowar (98.38%); 99.52 % area of Oilseeds majorly in Rapeseed & Mustard (99.85%); 92.00% of Wheat and 61.40% area of Rice has been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25. 3. Rabi Season Area Coverage: For Rabi horticulture crops, major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion – 12.58 lakh ha (9.76 lakh ha last year), Potato – 20.03 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato – 3.25 lakh ha (3.14 lakh ha last year). 4. Weather Update: a. Temperature: Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over Northwest India during next 3 days and fall by 2-4°C for subsequent 3 days. Gradual fall in maximum temperatures by 3-5°C likely over East India during next 2 Days and no significant change during subsequent 4 days. b. Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01– 28 April, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 15% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -27%; (ii) Northwest India: -34%; (iii) Central India: 6%; and South Peninsula: 54%. An active fresh Western Disturbance likely to impact Northwest India from 02nd May. Isolated hailstorm activity likely over Chhattisgarh on 28th; Odisha on 28th & 29th April and over North Interior Karnataka on 30th April & 01st May. Isolated heavy rainfall likely over Gangetic West Bengal on 28th; over

Isolated to scattered light rainfall with thunderstorm, lightning & strong winds likely over Western Himalayan region and plains of northwest India during 30th April to 03rd May. Inputs Situation a. Water Reservoir Status: As on 24th April 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 664.82 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 36% of total live storage capacity (182.37 BCM).The current year's storage is nearly 118 percent of last year's storage and 119 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. b. Groundwater Levels: Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014– 2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c. Seeds and Fertilizers: For Rabi 2024-25, certified seed availability is 337.98 lakh quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 6. Pests & Diseases: Intensity of pests and diseases, at some fields, has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Coconut (Stem bleeding, Ganoderma wilt, Rugose spiraling whitefly, Leaf blight ) in Karnataka and (Rugose Spiralling Whitefly) in Kerala. The Advisory has been issued by the survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level. 7. 1. RAINFALL

During the week (17th – 23rd April 2025), higher rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 25%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01th Mar to 24th April 2025) is lower than LPA by 15%.

content.text: Rainfall Forecast: 24 April – 30 April 2025 An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over north Bangladesh and another over northeast Assam in lower tropospheric levels. A north-south trough runs from central Chhattisgarh to Gulf of Mannar in lower tropospheric levels. A fresh Western Disturbance seen as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies: Isolated to scattered light rainfall with thunderstorm & lightning likely over Western Himalayan Region during 24th -26th April. No significant weather likely over rest parts of the country during the week. 01 May – 07 May 2025 Under the influence of western disturbances, isolated to scattered rainfall is likely over Western Himalayan Region during some days of the week. Due to trough/cyclonic circulations over East India, light/moderate scattered to fairly widespread rainfall along with thunderstorm & lightening are likely overeast & northeast India during some/many days of the week. Isolated heavy rainfall is also likely over northeast India during some days of the week. Due to trough/cyclonic circulations over Central & Peninsular India, Light/moderate rainfall along with thunderstorm & lightening also likely over central & south Peninsular
